record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let X be an affine scheme with coordinate algebra A, let Γ act on X and on a target algebra by automorphisms, and define the corresponding equivariant map algebra as the Γ-fixed subalgebra of target ⊗ A. Develop the representation theory of such equivariant map algebras when the target algebra is much more general than the finite-dimensional Lie or associative cases, including infinite-dimensional Lie targets such as Kac-Moody or Heisenberg algebras and non-Lie targets such as alternative or Jordan algebras. In cases where finite-dimensional representations are defined, describe those representations.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(b) More general targets. There are many possible choices for the “target” alge- bra g for which the resulting EMA has not been studied. Even in the setting of Lie algebras, one could consider g to be, for instance, a Kac-Moody algebra (see [ERF] for the untwisted multiloop case) or some other well-studied infinite-dimensional Lie algebra, such as the Heisenberg algebra.

In fact, one can study the representation theory of any EMA for which the target is an algebra with well-defined representations. For example, it would be natural to consider the finite-dimensional representations in the case of alternative algebras or Jordan algebras.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, with coordinate algebra $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$. Let $\Gamma$ be a group acting on $X$ by automorphisms, and let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a $k$-algebra (not necessarily a finite-dimensional Lie algebra or finite-dimensional associative algebra) equipped with an action of $\Gamma$ by algebra automorphisms. The action of $\Gamma$ on $X$ induces an action on $A$, and one forms the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A$. Define the equivariant map algebra
$$M(\mathfrak{g}, A)^\Gamma = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^\Gamma,$$
the subalgebra of $\Gamma$-fixed points.

Develop the representation theory of $M(\mathfrak{g}, A)^\Gamma$ in the following more general settings, in each case where a class of representations of $\mathfrak{g}$ is well-defined (in particular, classify or describe the finite-dimensional representations when those make sense):

(a) $\mathfrak{g}$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra, for example a (symmetrizable) Kac–Moody algebra or a Heisenberg algebra;

(b) $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-associative, non-Lie algebra admitting a meaningful representation theory, for example an alternative algebra or a Jordan algebra.

Provide, in each setting, a description of the irreducible (and, where appropriate, the finite-dimensional irreducible) representations of $M(\mathfrak{g}, A)^\Gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad research program proposed as an open direction for equivariant map algebras with more general target algebras. While partial progress exists in adjacent settings — e.g., quantization and Drinfeld-polynomial-style classifications for certain map algebras related to affine Kac–Moody parabolics, representations of loop Kac–Moody Lie algebras, and equivariant K-theory/twisted Heisenberg connections — there is no general representation theory of equivariant map algebras with Kac–Moody, Heisenberg, alternative, or Jordan targets. The overall program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Representations of Loop Kac-Moody Lie Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies representations in the untwisted loop Kac-Moody case, a special instance of the broader equivariant map algebra setting.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results exist for Kac-Moody targets (loop case), not the general equivariant case.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant K-theory, wreath products, and Heisenberg algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Equivariant K-groups carry a Hopf algebra structure isomorphic to a Fock space of a twisted Heisenberg superalgebra.
status_evidence.claim: Heisenberg-target connections appear only in adjacent contexts, not as a general representation theory of equivariant map algebras.

status_evidence.title: An update on Heisenberg and Kac-Moody categorification
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) survey of categorification activity for Heisenberg and Kac-Moody algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing activity but no general classification for equivariant map algebras with such targets.
